literal: And producing, and gathering, and guarding, and distributing the guarded (wealth), is what a capable government does.
translation: An able government is one that can generate wealth, gather it, safeguard it, and distribute what has been safeguarded.
modern: பொருளை உருவாக்கும் வழிகளை அறிதலும், அவ்வாறு வரும் பொருளைச் சேர்த்தலும், சேர்த்த பொருளைக் காத்தலும், காத்த பொருளைத் திட்டமிட்டுப் பகிர்ந்தளித்தலும் வல்லதே சிறந்த அரசு ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the four essential economic duties of an effective state or ruler. First, 'iyaṟṟal' refers to creating or identifying new sources of revenue. Second, 'īṭṭal' is the actual collection and accumulation of these resources into the treasury. Third, 'kāttal' is safeguarding the collected wealth from external threats, waste, or corruption. Finally, 'vakuttal' is the wise allocation and distribution of the protected wealth for public welfare, defense, and development. A state that excels in all four of these functions is deemed capable and successful.
